data.title: Swiss Market Ends Notably Lower
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - The Switzerland stock market ended weak on Friday after remaining in negative territory throughout the session, amid a sell-off in global equity markets amid concerns about returns on AI-related investments.

The benchmark SMI ended with a loss of 171.23 points or 1.14% at 14,796.50, the day's high. The index touched a low of 14,596.21 in the session.

Sandoz Group, up marginally, was the only gainer in the SMI index. Amrize, Roche and Julius Baer settled modestly lower.

Swiss RE ended down 4.55%. Kuehne + Nagel drifted lower by nearly 4%. Alcon, Lindt & Spruengli, Zurich Insurance and Helvetia Baloise Holding dropped 2%-2.5%.

Swisscom, Schindler Ps, Sika, Geberit, Galderma Group, Swiss Life Holding, Logitech International, SGS, Nestle, Sonova, Lonza Group, Straumann Holding and Givaudan ended lower by 1.2%-2%.

Survey data from the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, or SECO, showed consumers in Switzerland remained more pessimistic in October, with the confidence level weakening to the lowest level in nearly three years.

The consumer sentiment index dropped to -45 in October from -37 in the corresponding month last year. The index also worsened from -36 in September. The expected score was -35.0.

data.title: Eyes on next week's tech results after recent selloff
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq, S&P 500 higher; Dow dips
  • Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; consumer staples down most
  • Dollar, US crude gain; gold, bitcoin down
  • US 10-yr Treasury yield up at 4.85%

EYES ON NEXT WEEK'S TECH RESULTS AFTER RECENT SELLOFF

The bulk of third-quarter S&P 500 earnings reports are in, but Thursday's sharp tech-led selloff and worries about increased AI regulations may keep investors closely focused on results ahead from some key tech companies.

Results from CoreWeave , Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are all due next week, while top chipmaker Nvidia is due to release its quarterly report on November 17.

Strategists said the AI trade worries followed Tuesday's midterm elections, where Democrats won control of the US Congress and also won several key governors' races in data-center-heavy states such as Texas. Voters have been concerned for months about environmental and other issues due to the rise of data centers. The tech-heavy Nasdaq had its biggest daily percentage drop in 19 months on Thursday, confirming it was in a correction.

Year-over-year earnings growth for the third quarter for S&P 500 CBOE:SPX companies is now estimated at 33.4%, according to LSEG data on Friday, which is based on results from 435 of the companies. The latest estimate is up from 30.6% at the start of October.

data.title: Congo says China's Huayou unit must pay $6 million compensation despite halt
data.description:
Chinese-owned miner CDM must still pay $6 million to Congolese communities hit by last year's industrial wastewater spill even though it has suspended operations, the Democratic Republic of Congo's mines ministry said on Friday.

Congo is the world's largest cobalt producer and second-largest copper producer, and has tightened mining regulations in recent years to boost state revenues.

Congo Dongfang International Mining (CDM) is a unit of China's Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt , one of the world's largest battery materials producers and a key supplier to the electric vehicle industry.

Congolese authorities suspended CDM for three months after wastewater leaked from a containment basin at its Lubumbashi operation in November 2025, contaminating nearby communities. The basin was designed for water retention but had been used to store acidic solutions.

Authorities subsequently ordered the company to pay $2 million each to the three affected communities of Kasapa, Kamatete and Kamisepe.

In a statement on Friday, the mines ministry said implementation of the compensation programme had been delayed in part by financial difficulties cited by CDM, which recently announced a suspension of its activities.

"Financial difficulties or the suspension of operations do not exempt the operator from its obligations toward affected populations," the ministry said.

Commitments made to local communities "must be honoured", it added.

Huayou and CDM did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The ministry said CDM was also required to pay a $6.6 million penalty to the state treasury following the incident.
